evidence.claim: MP Materials' SEC filing says it owns and operates a Fort Worth rare earth metal, alloy and magnet manufacturing facility and commenced NdFeB permanent magnet manufacturing in December 2025; it also describes an estimated expansion path to 10,000 MT per year of US rare earth magnet capacity.
MP Materials describes its Independence facility in Fort Worth, Texas as a fully integrated facility for producing NdFeB permanent magnets, including alloy flake, magnet block, and finished magnets.

Energy Fuels announced that 99.9% purity dysprosium oxide produced at its White Mesa Mill passed initial purity and QA/QC processes of a major South Korean permanent magnet manufacturer, with terbium and potentially samarium oxide expected in early 2026.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels' US-Produced Heavy Rare Earth Oxide Successfully Qualified for Use in Permanent Magnets

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels said it was planning to install large-scale dysprosium, terbium, and potentially other heavy rare earth oxide production capacity at White Mesa by Q4 2026, while also warning that these plans are forward-looking.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels Successfully Produces First Kilogram of 99.9% Purity Dysprosium Oxide at its White Mesa Mill in Utah

evidence.claim: Neo Performance Materials announced commissioning of a heavy rare earth separation production line in Europe that produced separated terbium and dysprosium process solutions from mixed rare earth carbonate feedstock, with processing completed entirely in Europe.
evidence.source_title: Neo Successfully Commissions Heavy Rare Earth Separation Production Line in Europe

evidence.claim: Neo stated that its heavy rare earth separation initiative complements its European permanent magnet facility in Estonia, which is advancing through customer qualification milestones with commercial production expected to ramp later in 2026.
evidence.source_title: Neo Successfully Commissions Heavy Rare Earth Separation Production Line in Europe

evidence.claim: Critical Metals describes the Tanbreez rare earth project as containing heavy rare earth elements and other key minerals in eudialyte, with an average grade of 0.4% total rare earth oxides including 27% heavy rare earth oxides.

Critical Metals could become a non-Chinese heavy-rare-earth feedstock contributor, but the evidence provided here does not yet prove defense qualification, separated oxide production, or magnet-chain qualification.
evidence.source_title: Critical Metals Corp Corporate Presentation April 23, 2025

evidence.claim: CNAS argues that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile and that DoD and primes often lack visibility below tier two, supporting the Serenity lens that subtier suppliers and hidden chokepoints can be missed by headline defense analysis.

memory_update.text: MP remains the reference anchor for US mine-to-magnet integration, but its high attention level makes it less useful for the underfollowed lane except as a benchmark for qualification, capacity, and feedstock compliance.

Energy Fuels should be tracked as a heavy-rare-earth oxide bottleneck candidate rather than only as a uranium name; key survival test is repeated Dy/Tb magnet qualification and commercial-scale non-Chinese feedstock.

Neo Performance Materials is a strong underfollowed OTC/Canadian-listed allied magnet-chain candidate because it combines Estonia separation, heavy REE work, magnetic materials, and permanent magnet qualification milestones.

Critical Metals is a speculative-shadow upstream feedstock candidate; keep only if later evidence shows viable processing, financing, offtake, and qualification into Western oxide or magnet supply chains.

For this node, the highest-value evidence is not mining resource size alone; it is proof of non-Chinese feedstock origin, separated NdPr/Dy/Tb oxide quality, metal/alloy conversion, magnet production, and customer or defense-prime qualification.

Need a later pass on private and non-US-listed chokepoints such as USA Rare Earth, Vulcan Elements, Lynas, VAC, Arnold Magnetic, REalloys, and alloy/metallization equipment vendors; they may explain which public names receive offtake or toll-processing demand.

node: Rare-earth magnets and non-Chinese feedstock qualification for defense systems
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the chokepoint hypothesis that defense-relevant rare-earth magnet exposure is less about headline mine ownership and more about qualified non-Chinese oxide, heavy rare earth, metal/alloy, and magnet-chain capacity. The pass keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, then prioritizes underfollowed or narrower public names tied to separated oxides, heavy rare earths, European/Western magnet conversion, and future non-Chinese feedstock qualification. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
